scope_warning: DEVELOPMENT experiment. These are the 32 development seeds used for lambda selection. This is NOT a paper-level generalisation claim; the untouched 10300001..10300192 block gets the final word.
why_this_control_matters: after discovering that EXP2B and EXP2C never maintained their stated assigned-pole treatment (occupancy at chance), this lambda_R = 0 run is the FIRST clean test of z0 <-> A and z1 <-> B with persistent assignment and NO payoff-ranking loss.
finding: Under corrected persistent assigned-pole training with lambda_R = 0, the latent policy recovered the intended strategic ordering on pole A (delta_A = +0.1063) but NOT on pole B (delta_B = -0.0249) on the frozen development block. Persistent assignment alone was therefore insufficient to recover both strategic contrasts in this development experiment.
asymmetry: z0 dominates on pole A, but z1 does NOT beat z0 on pole B. Roughly half the intended ordering appears from persistence alone.

what_the_ranking_objective_adds.observed: delta_B is flipped into the desired direction at EVERY nonzero lambda
what_the_ranking_objective_adds.pattern: ranking pressure immediately repairs B, while stronger pressure gradually restores the A contrast that weaker pressure initially damages. At lambda = 1.0 both exceed the control for the first time in the grid.
what_the_ranking_objective_adds.not_purchased_with_return: every treatment EXCEEDED the control's development return (0.078-0.105 vs 0.045), so the 5% degradation constraint never bound.

hypothesis_for_production: Persistent assignment establishes part of the strategic structure; sufficiently strong payoff-ranking pressure may repair the missing response ordering without sacrificing task performance. The untouched 192-seed block now gets to falsify this.
